banner: SNIPER KILL-SWITCH SPEC (LOCAL DESIGN ARTIFACT — NOT A LIVE CONTROL)
disclaimers: SNIPER KILL-SWITCH SPEC — a machine-readable LOCAL design/checklist artifact describing what a future kill switch must do. It is NOT a kill switch.
It performs NO process control: nothing here stops, starts, signals, or monitors any process, and it exposes no live controls.
The stop-live-disabled-placeholder mode is PERMANENTLY disabled in v1 — Phase 7 (live/burner trading) is not started and cannot be controlled from here.
The Phase-6 prerequisite tracker consumes this artifact; an adopted spec is a PREREQUISITE for future simulation work, never authorization for it.
No wallet, key, signing, sending, or transaction planning is involved anywhere in this artifact.

modes.description: halt all NEW paper decision builds for the session (existing artifacts stay readable)
halt any future Phase 6 simulation run before it starts (Phase 6 is not implemented yet — this mode is specified ahead of it)
PERMANENTLY DISABLED placeholder for a future live halt — Phase 7 is not started and cannot be controlled from here

requiredOperatorConfirmations: rehearsal-operator confirms adoption of the canonical PAPER-only kill-switch spec for this dry run
the operator explicitly confirms the session label being halted
the operator explicitly confirms which mode is being tripped
disabledActions: building any new paper decision report
building or diffing any simulation intent plan
any future live/burner action (already disabled by design)
auditRequirements: every trip and reset must be recorded in a local audit artifact with the operator label
the tripped mode and the reason must be recorded verbatim
testRequirements: a test must prove a tripped switch refuses every disabled action
a test must prove the live placeholder mode cannot be armed
warnings: no escalation notes — consider writing down who to alert when the switch trips.
notes: This artifact is a SPEC: it controls nothing, halts nothing, and exposes no live behaviour.
The three modes are fixed in v1; the live mode is a permanently-disabled placeholder.
